area: Adversarial review of the _agent-guidance#58 spec (federated skills.lock re-pinning: generator `--repin-source` in agentskills + the nightly bumper in _agent-guidance)

findings.claim: KILLER — the spec's bumper step 1 ("Hoist the federated check out of the `current_exit -eq 0` branch") produces a `fed_drifted` flag that is TRUE WHENEVER THE PRIMARY DRIFTED, because the full-lock `--check-current` emits one combined `FAILED:` across primary + every source. Wired to the spec's step 4 (`--repin-source "$reg@"` for every entry of `source_registries`), the result is: on every routine nightly where the primary bundle content moved, EVERY federated pin is advanced to its checkout's HEAD. That is precisely the harm ADR 0005 and `test_repin_on_a_federated_lock_preserves_every_source_verbatim` exist to prevent, delivered by the PR that claims to preserve them. The spec files the imprecision only under N>1 sources and calls it "not reachable today"; the primary-vs-federated ambiguity IS reachable today, on both live federated locks (adamdaniel.ai, jodidaniel.com), every night the agentskills bundle moves.
findings.evidence:
My repro at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/hoist — two real git registries, lock federating `cms-platform`, then ONLY the primary edited and committed; the federated source left exactly at its pin:
  $ python3 .../generate_skills_lock.py --check-current --repo primary -o lock.json
  FAILED: the bundle has moved on since bfe087351201e57c91d4b54cb79d127026f451c2, which lock.json still pins — ...
    - changed: 'adam/alpha' differs from its content at bfe087351201...
  FULL EXIT=1
The federated source contributed zero differences, yet the run is `FAILED:` and exit 1 — the exact signal the spec's hoist reads as fed_drifted.
The script already says this in its own words. bump-consumer-locks.sh:911-919: "THE QUESTION IS SCOPED TO THE PRIMARY, and that is the design rather than an optimisation. --check-current reads EVERY source a lock names and emits one FAILED: for the whole run if any of them differs ... Handing the generator a copy of the lock with `sources` removed asks a different QUESTION rather than reinterpreting the combined answer". test/run-tests.sh:945-947 repeats it for the fixture: "The gate reads the primary alone; a combined verdict would re-pin...". The spec cites :912-919 as "the standing argument" for a scoping primitive and then does not apply it to its own hoist.
findings.proposedChange:
Do not hoist. Gate on a SCOPED question, symmetric to the existing `primary_only` helper (bump-consumer-locks.sh:233). Add the scoping primitive to PR 1 rather than deferring it: `--check-current --only <registry>` in generate_skills_lock.py, filtering `sources` in `check_current` (:1153) to the named source before the loop, erroring if the registry is not one this lock plans. Then in the bumper run `--check-current --only "$reg"` once per entry of `source_registries` and set `fed_drifted_regs+=("$reg")` only for the ones that individually return `^FAILED:`, and pass `--repin-source` for exactly those. Never derive federated drift from the combined exit code, and never by parsing the output (:911-919).
Locking test, in test/run-tests.sh: extend the spec's own new `bumporg/repo-fed-stale` fixture so its federated source is CURRENT while the primary is stale, and assert the resulting PR's lock has `sources[0].ref` unchanged at `$BUMP_SRC_REF` while the top-level `ref` advanced. Without that negative control the hoist bug ships green — every existing federated assertion (:3790-3801) is about the primary-current case only.

findings.claim: The proposed implementation contradicts its own proposed test. The spec enumerates the generator changes exhaustively ("`--repin-source` argparse entry + `parse_repin_source` + `_apply_repin_sources` + the merge call after line 1535") and NEVER implements the refusal that `test_repin_source_without_repin_is_an_argparse_error` asserts. Worse, the guard it does specify is `if args.repin_source:` — not `if args.repin and args.repin_source:` — so `--repin-source` silently fires on a PLAIN GENERATE, mutating a source in the one operation the spec says only `--repin` may perform.
findings.evidence:
Spec text, finding (a2) proposedChange: "Insert a merge step in `main()` AFTER line 1535 ... `if args.repin_source: extras = _apply_repin_sources(...)`". Nothing else is listed.
The existing post-parse refusal it would have to join is generate_skills_lock.py:1403-1417, and its list is exactly `("--registry", args.registry), ("--bundles", args.bundles), ("--source", args.source)` — verified verbatim.
Two counterexamples against the spec as written:
(1) `--registry X --ref R --bundles adam --source 'b=owner/o@<40hex>:skills' --repin-source 'owner/o@'` — no `--repin`. `extras` comes from `--source` (:1513-1514), the guard fires, `_apply_repin_sources` advances the source. Exit 0, no refusal.
(2) `--repin-source 'owner/other@'` with no `--source` and no `--repin` — `extras = []` (:1533), so `_apply_repin_sources` raises GeneratorError "is not a source this lock federates (none)". GeneratorError exits **1**, not argparse's 2: generate_skills_lock.py:1651-1655 `except GeneratorError as error: sys.exit(f"ERROR: {error}")`. The spec's test expects an argparse error, so it fails against the spec's own code.
findings.proposedChange:
Fold the refusal into the existing block at :1403-1417 as a distinct post-parse check, and tighten the guard:
```python
    if args.repin_source and not args.repin:
        parser.error(
            "--repin-source advances a pin the lock already carries, so it only means "
            "anything alongside --repin; a plain generate states its sources with --source.")
```
and at the merge site `if args.repin and args.repin_source:`. Belt and braces, because the two guards fail differently: the parser.error is the exit-2 contract the test asserts, the tightened guard is what makes counterexample (1) unrepresentable even if a later editor moves the parse. Keep `--repin-source` OUT of the `overriding` list — the spec is right that it must never be folded in there, and its `test_repin_source_is_not_in_the_refused_identity_flags` is the correct lock for that.

findings.claim: The test the spec calls "the whole point" has no fixture and cannot be written as scoped. It says all new generator tests go "on the existing `federated` fixture", then names `test_repin_source_advances_only_the_named_source` — "(two-source lock; the unnamed one comes back byte-identical — this is the merge-not-replace property and the whole point)". The `federated` fixture builds exactly ONE extra source. No fixture anywhere in the file builds two real federated checkouts.
findings.evidence:
scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py:406-416 — `federated` returns `(primary, primary_sha, extra, extra_sha)`, a single sibling registry `cms-platform`; `_federated_lock` (:419-426) emits exactly one `--source`.
Grep for every `--source` occurrence in the file (13 hits) shows the only multi-source invocation is :773-778, inside `attempt(count)`, which builds `--source b{N}=owner/extra{N}@{'%040d' % N}:skills` — fake registries, fake zero-padded shas, no checkouts on disk. Its own docstring (:765-768) says the at-cap run "must get far enough to fail for an unrelated reason (no checkout at the sibling path)", i.e. it deliberately never resolves a second source. It asserts only `MAX_SOURCES` (=8, generate_skills_lock.py:382).
So merge-not-replace across two live sources is untestable on the fixtures the spec names, and the spec budgets no new fixture.
findings.proposedChange: Add a `federated_two` fixture beside `federated` (:406) building a SECOND sibling registry — e.g. `tmp_path / "other-platform"` via `make_registry(..., {"other/publish": SKILL_C}, layout="skills")` — with a bundle name and skill basenames that collide with neither `adam/alpha` nor `cms-platform/deploy`, since `_reject_basename_collisions` (generate_skills_lock.py:834) is a hard error on a shared basename and would mask the property under test. Give it a `_federated_two_lock` helper emitting both `--source` specs. Then `test_repin_source_advances_only_the_named_source` asserts the un-named source's dict is `==` its pre-repin dict (all four SOURCE_FIELDS), not merely that `ref` is unchanged. The single-source `federated` fixture is still the right home for the refusal tests and for `test_repin_source_with_an_empty_ref_advances_to_that_sources_head` (advance it with the `_git(extra, "commit", ...)` + `_head()` pattern already used at :634-635 and :2215).

findings.claim: MISSED ENTIRELY: advancing a federated pin makes two hard-failure paths reachable in the nightly that cannot fire today, both of which turn the scheduled run RED rather than degrading. The spec proposes no fixture, no test and no mention for either. Combined with finding 1, they become reachable on nights when no federated source drifted at all.
findings.evidence:
(a) Basename collision. `--repin` rebuilds every digest: build_lock -> plan_sources -> collect_from_sources -> `_reject_basename_collisions` (generate_skills_lock.py:823-834), whose docstring says "Federating a second registry is what makes this reachable at all". If the advanced source's bundle gained a skill directory whose basename matches one in the primary, `--repin` raises. The bumper then hits bump-consumer-locks.sh:1149 `fail "$repo_name: --repin failed — ..."` with `((FAIL_COUNT++))`, and the run's only non-zero exit is `[[ $FAIL_COUNT -gt 0 ]]` at the tail.
(b) Bundle shrink. `skills_shrink_reason` (bump-consumer-locks.sh:253-281) groups by `key.split("/", 1)[0]` across the WHOLE lock, so a rename/delete/layout change in the FEDERATED bundle now yields "bundle(s) cms-platform lost every skill they had" -> :1171 `fail "$repo_name: refusing to propose this re-pin ..."` + `((FAIL_COUNT++))`.
Neither is reachable today for a federated bundle: the comment at :877-882 states "--repin advances ONLY the primary ref, but it re-derives EVERY digest, including each federated source's at that source's own unchanged pin" — unchanged is the load-bearing word, and the spec's change removes it.
findings.proposedChange: State both in the spec as expected new failure modes and decide the policy explicitly: a red nightly for a cross-registry basename collision or a vanished federated bundle is arguably correct (a human must decide), but it must be a decision with a test, not a surprise. Add two fixtures to `setup_bump_repos()` in test/run-tests.sh: one where advancing the federated source introduces a basename already in the primary bundle, asserting the run FAILs with the collision named and `assert_no_bump_branch`; one where the federated bundle is emptied at HEAD, asserting the `refusing to propose this re-pin` path fires and the lock on the default branch is untouched. If a red nightly is judged too blunt for a source the bumper chose to advance on its own initiative, the alternative is to drop that source's `--repin-source` and re-run, reporting it — but that must be written down, not left to whichever branch happens to be hit first.

findings.claim: Factually wrong contract handed to the PR-2 implementer: "the bumper never parses [--check-current output] beyond `grep -q '^FAILED:'` (:953, :1055)". It also slices the output from `^FAILED:` to end-of-output and embeds it in the PR body, capped at 20 lines, with a `sed` substitution keyed to `$primary_lock` specifically. The merge-order conclusion survives (that call uses the primary-scoped lock, so exactly one block prints), but two consequences the spec asserts away do bite PR 2.
findings.evidence:
bump-consumer-locks.sh:1360:
  $(sed -n '/^FAILED:/,$p' <<< "$check_out" | head -20 | sed "s#$primary_lock#$LOCK_REL_PATH#g")
and the parallel :1331 for `$format_out`. `$check_out` is the primary-scoped run (`-o "$primary_lock"`, :937-939); `$fed_out` is the FULL-lock run (`-o "$lock_file"`, :948-951).
Consequence 1: the spec's per-source report prints headline + 3 continuation lines + remediation + N difference lines PER drifted source. `head -20` will truncate a multi-block report mid-block in a PR body.
Consequence 2: any attempt to quote `$fed_out` in the body (which the spec's step 6 `federated_note` rewrite invites) leaks the absolute `$lock_file` path, because the only substitution present names `$primary_lock`.
findings.proposedChange: Correct the spec's cross-repo contract to: the bumper branches on `grep -q '^FAILED:'` AND quotes from `^FAILED:` onward into the PR body under a 20-line cap, with `$primary_lock` path-substituted. So PR 1's hard constraint is not just "`FAILED:` at column 0" — it is also that the PRIMARY block must stay first and self-contained within its first few lines. Add a test in scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py asserting the primary block's headline and its `--repin` remediation appear within the first 5 lines of a multi-source FAILED report, so the `head -20` slice can never carry a headline without its own remediation line. In PR 2, if `$fed_out` is ever quoted, extend the substitution to `sed -e "s#$primary_lock#$LOCK_REL_PATH#g" -e "s#$lock_file#$LOCK_REL_PATH#g"`.

openQuestions: Sound parts, so they are not re-litigated: findings (a) and (b) are correctly evidenced — I re-read generate_skills_lock.py:1403-1417, :1506, :1512-1532, :828 and :1138-1186 verbatim and they say what the spec says; the spec's own repro at scratchpad/test_repro.py carries 5 real asserts on the load-bearing facts (frozen source ref, silent exit 0, --check-current exit 1, argparse exit 2), so its "exit 0" is not a hollow verifier. Both baselines reproduce exactly: agentskills `python3 -m pytest scripts/ plugins/*/skills/*/tests/ plugins/*/skills/*/scripts/ -q` -> 962 passed, EXIT=0 (unpiped); _agent-guidance `bash test/run-tests.sh` -> 441 passed, 7 failed, EXIT=1, all 7 `node_modules/yaml is missing`. The rejection of option 1 is right and well-argued. The `report_digest_format` doc-debt item is real and still unfixed — generate_skills_lock.py:1089-1096 still says "the bumper's OWN re-pin passes no `--ref`", which bump-consumer-locks.sh:1139-1142 falsified. The merge order (agentskills first, soft probe) is right for the reason given.

Internal contradiction in the risk sizing the spec leans on. Finding (d) says the federated locks are "2 sources each", the bumper proposal says "Both federated locks in this fleet carry exactly one source, so it is not reachable today". These reconcile only if "2 sources" means plan_sources' primary+extra. An implementer sizing the N>1 exposure cannot tell which was meant, and it is the sentence the whole precision-limit waiver rests on. Restate it as "two federated locks, one federated source each (plus the primary)" — or drop the waiver, since finding 1 shows the imprecision is reachable at N=1 anyway.

I could not close the spec's own open question 1. The session connector is scoped to the same three repos, so agentskills-private, repo-settings, claude-memory-map, fastmail-actions and scratch-claude-002 are still unread here. Per AGENTS.md a 404 on the org connector means "not visible to this credential", not "absent". Still worth one `gh api` pass from a credential that can see them before PR 1.

The three inline stub generators in test/run-tests.sh (argparse at :4042-4045, :4608-4613, :4685-4691) are additional to `write_stub_generator` (:649), and the spec mentions only the last. I checked and they are not blockers — the :4042 one lacks `--repin` so the run exits 2 at the load-bearing probe (bump-consumer-locks.sh:638-641) before the loop, and :4608/:4685 run against the single non-federated `repo-bare-old-gen`, so the hoist is a no-op there. But the spec's new soft probe will emit a `::warning::` in all three tests' logs; confirm no assertion in those lanes is sensitive to it, and add the three to the spec's stub inventory so the next flag does not have to rediscover them.

Whether a red nightly is the right response to the two newly-reachable hard failures in finding 4 (cross-registry basename collision; federated bundle emptied at HEAD) is a policy call the spec never surfaces. It belongs in the new ADR 0009 alongside the supersession of ADR 0005's Left-open bullet, not in whichever branch of bump-consumer-locks.sh happens to be reached first.
